title: Evals-driven regression notifications and console routing for model/config changes
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add first-class integration between Evals results and the Console alerting surface so that model or configuration changes that cause quality regressions trigger actionable notifications. This ticket scopes the product requirements and acceptance criteria for: 1) tying eval runs to specific model/config rollouts, 2) configurable alert thresholds and severity mapping, 3) deduplicated notification grouping in Slack and PagerDuty, and 4) quick links in notifications to rollback/playbook/runbook items and relevant PRs or rollout controls. The goal is to reduce time-to-detect and time-to-remediate quality regressions introduced by model swaps, quantization changes, or altered inference settings (e.g., max_tokens, sampling).
acceptance_criteria: Eval runs can be annotated with metadata: model_id, model_version, config_snapshot_id, rollout_id, and eval_suite_id
Console shows an Evals Regression card per model+eval_suite with a 7-day baseline and delta visualized, and a link to the failing prompt set
Users can configure severity rules in Console mapping eval metrics and % delta to alert tiers (info/warn/critical) per project
When a rule fires, a single grouped notification is sent to configured Slack channels and PagerDuty services, consolidating multiple alerts for the same rollout within a 30-minute window
Notifications include: short summary, top N failing examples, metric diffs, model/config identifiers, link to eval run details, link to rollout controls, and suggested remediation steps
Console UI allows manual suppression or muting for a specific rollout or model for a defined window (e.g., 1h/24h), and records the action in audit logs
Alert routing respects customer subscriptions and per-team PagerDuty mappings configured in Console; test alert flow validated end-to-end in staging
Alert history and dedupe metrics are visible in the Console incident timeline, and we can export alert events to observability pipelines
On-call PagerDuty incidents created by eval regressions include a link that opens a pre-populated Github/PR checklist for rollback or canary adjustments
implementation_notes: Source of truth: tie each eval run to a config_snapshot stored in the model registry; config_snapshot includes inference flags, quantization profile, and pinned tokenizer
Dedupe key: use a hash of (org_id, model_id, config_snapshot_id, eval_suite_id, metric_name) and a sliding window to group related regressions
Severity mapping: default thresholds are provided (e.g., >5% drop for warn, >12% drop for critical) but are editable per project
Notification payloads: send concise blocks to Slack (channel + thread) and create PagerDuty events with dedup_key set to dedupe hash
Backfill: when enabling for a project, run historical evals to seed baselines and avoid noisy first-run alerts
Privacy: do not include raw user data in notifications — only anonymized failing prompts and synthetic reproductions; ensure KMS masking rules applied
Observability: emit metrics for alerts_fired, alerts_deduped, alerts_suppressed, and mean_time_to_ack per project
Docs + Runbooks: create a Console help page and an on-call runbook template for handling eval regressions
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): wire Evals -> Console events for a small internal project; validate Slack and PagerDuty end-to-end (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (alpha): opt-in for 3 customer projects with manual threshold tuning and collect feedback (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (beta): default enable with conservative thresholds, add UI for severity rules and suppression, and support export to external observability (4 weeks)
Phase 4 (GA): enable self-serve configuration in Console, publish docs and runbooks, iterate on UX for failing example triage (2 weeks)
Monitoring: monitor false-positive rate and alerts-per-day; target <1 actionable alert per model per week at GA
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy first-run alerts when baselines are not established. Mitigation: require backfill and baseline stabilization before firing high-severity alerts.
Risk: alert storms for widespread changes (e.g., infra causing upstream tokenization differences). Mitigation: global suppression toggle and rapid blast radius controls in Console.
Risk: leaking PII in failing examples. Mitigation: auto-mask according to data classification rules and limit examples to synthetic reproductions where possible.
Risk: misrouted PagerDuty incidents. Mitigation: validate per-team mappings in staging with synthetic alerts and fail open to email only if mappings missing.
